title: 8 Tiffin Boxes? Power Sets Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Aarav has three snacks: a samosa, a banana and a laddoo. How many different tiffin boxes can he pack, counting the empty one? Every box is a subset, and the set of all of them is the power set. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (Chapter 1, Sets) we learn what a power set is and why a set with n elements has 2 to the power n subsets. Note: the power set is not in the current NCERT text, but it is still in the JEE Main syllabus.

You will watch a live tree double the number of boxes as each snack is added (1, 2, 4, 8), flip one in-or-out switch per element through all eight boxes, and compare A with P(A) side by side. There is a pause-and-think question on P(φ), a worked example that lists P({1, 2}), the exam trap of forgetting φ and A itself, an original JEE Main pattern question on P(P(A)) with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
